question: Upstream #12741 reports a long tool loop that finishes a turn with no visible reply: the UI accepts a final step only when it has visible text and no tool-call block, while a tool result can mark the turn concluded. Does a local tool whose success calls `concludeTurn()` end a `completed` turn on a step that carries a text block and a tool call, and does the scanner count that shape without stealing the no-answer count?

probe.homes: .tmp/r65-runs/conclude and .tmp/r65-runs/control (one isolated DSH_HOME; nothing under ~/.dsh is written)
probe.endpoint: a local OpenAI-compatible server: the first step streams one text delta and one `probe_conclude` tool call, then `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`; a tool-result request streams text only
probe.why_the_shape_survives: `dsh-agent-loop/src/agent.ts` returns `{kind:"completed"}` from a step with tool calls when the batch result is `concluded` (`toolCalls.length === 0` / `result.concluded ? {kind:"completed"} : null`), and `dsh-tools` carries that marker from `ToolRunContext.concludeTurn()`. The UI rule is `dsh-client-ui-chat/.../turn-process.ts:160-161`: a final step with any tool-call block is not a final answer, even when it also has text.
probe.note: the endpoint is local and synthetic: it reproduces the host mechanism, not a relay incident

findings: A tool result that calls `concludeTurn()` ends the turn `completed` on a step that still carries a tool call, so the last assistant message can be `["text","tool-call"]`.
The control run, same endpoint, prompt and tool name with `concludeTurn()` off, takes a second step and ends on a text-only message; the only difference a reader can see is the concluding marker.

The scanner counts the conclude run and not the control; `completed_without_answer` stays zero, because P-0044 already counts the tool call as work. P-0052 adds the second count rather than redefining the first rule.
The host and UI lines that make the shape possible are quoted in `docs/patches/P-0052-completed-on-tool-call.md`; the local endpoint reproduces the mechanism, not an incident.
not_proven: The endpoint is local and synthetic. It reproduces the host mechanism, not a relay or model incident.
One route, one model, one prompt, one tool; a multi-tool batch and a multi-step conclusion were not exercised.
The desktop UI was not driven for this probe: both runs are headless CLI runs, and the "no reply" half is read from `turn-process.ts`, not observed on screen.
The number this artifact records is a transcript rule, not a count of user-visible incidents; the machine had produced zero of the shape before the probe.
